solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

blocks.note: to warp is to bend or swerve out of true
a lane is a channel, as a shipping lane

annotation.surface: A fighter pilot jinks sharply while crossing the English Channel.
annotation.walkthrough: Capital C makes 'Channel' look like the stretch of sea the Spitfire flew over; it is just a lane. The Spitfire was a British Second World War fighter.
annotation.definitionFit: The Spitfire is a famous example of a warplane, hence the question mark.

blocks.note: to set something down is to put it
rid = free, as in 'rid of the pests'

annotation.surface: Someone is released from confinement and emerges reeking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Set free' reads as one phrase meaning released, but it splits into two words that each supply a piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Putrid means rotten, and so smelling foul.

indicators.note: a chaotic putsch has its letters in disorder
the rearranged letters involve, take in, the other piece

blocks.note: PUTSCH rearranged
it = sex appeal, a crossword standard

annotation.surface: A disorderly coup attempt gets mixed up with a sex-and-money scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: A putsch is an attempted coup, so 'chaotic' looks like a description of it rather than an instruction to rearrange its letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A stitch-up is British slang for a con or a frame-up, a swindle.

blocks.note: the surface offers costumes in general, the wardrobe department of a television show
TV is also short for transvestite, so this is the clothing a cross-dresser wears

annotation.surface: A question about the costumes worn on television.
annotation.walkthrough: TV reads as television, but it is also short for transvestite: the clothing seen on a TV is drag.
annotation.definitionFit: Drag is clothing of the opposite sex, worn by a cross-dresser or drag performer.

blocks.note: read as a verb: to mushroom is to grow and extend rapidly
a paste you smear on toast with a knife

annotation.surface: A menu item: pâté made from mushrooms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' reads as a noun in a food scene, but here it is the verb: to mushroom is to spread rapidly.
annotation.definitionFit: Mushroom (verb) means spread fast; pâté is a spread you put on toast.

indicators.note: almost the word means all of it but the last letter

blocks.note: having no money; the last letter T goes

annotation.surface: Someone nearly bankrupt blows their disguise.
annotation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money. 'Broke cover' is a set phrase for leaving hiding, which hides the split.
annotation.definitionFit: Skin is the outer cover of a body or fruit.

indicators.note: some of a word is a run of its letters

blocks.note: aspaRAGUs

annotation.surface: A recipe note: a little asparagus goes into the Italian sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a plausible cooking tip, so 'some asparagus' reads as an ingredient quantity.
annotation.definitionFit: Ragù is an Italian meat sauce served with pasta.

entries.clue: Go and fish the American way? (8)

blocks.note: your go in a game is your turn
the pike is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: An invitation to go fishing as Americans do.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The American way' sounds like a manner of doing things; it is a road, a way, in America.
annotation.definitionFit: A turnpike is an American toll highway, so an American way in the road sense.

entries.clue: Leans back to welcome Irish character (6)

indicators.note: to lean back is to tilt the wrong way, and here the word itself tips over and reads backwards
the reversed word welcomes the other piece inside it

blocks.note: tips = leans, tilts
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

annotation.surface: Someone leans back in greeting to an Irish guest.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' reads as a person in the story, but it is the definition, meaning nature or pluck.
annotation.definitionFit: Spirit and character both mean a person's temperament or mettle.

definitions.note: the first definition is a cryptic description: greens are what golfers putt on

blocks.note: putting is the golf stroke played on the smooth short grass around the hole
leafy vegetables such as cabbage and kale

annotation.surface: Someone adds these vegetables to a dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Putting on' looks like adding to a plate; it is golf putting, done on the greens.
annotation.definitionFit: A putting green is where golfers putt, and greens are leafy vegetables.

blocks.note: a verb: to pass something over to someone
a manual labourer, as on a farm or a ship's deck
a third sense, as in 'lend me one', so the clue is really a triple definition

annotation.surface: An instruction to help out a worker.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one instruction, but every word is a separate meaning of the same short word.
annotation.definitionFit: Three everyday senses of one word: pass over, a manual labourer, and help.

entries.clue: Assassin in Edinburgh, not British, shot (5,3)

indicators.note: not British means take out B
shot means wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: EDINBURGH without B, the abbreviation for British

annotation.surface: A news line: a foreign hitman is gunned down in Edinburgh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' belongs to the assassin story, but it means 'ruined', as in 'my nerves are shot'.
annotation.definitionFit: A hired gun is someone paid to kill.

indicators.note: the letters are arranged badly, out of order
the rearranged letters go inside the other word

blocks.note: a lip is a rim, as of a cup
GROWN rearranged

annotation.surface: A sore has developed nastily on someone's lip.
annotation.walkthrough: Lip reads as the mouth, where infections do appear; here it is the rim of a vessel.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: despite its name, ringworm is a fungus, not a worm, spreading over the skin in ring-shaped patches.

entries.clue: On warpath fix weapon American bears (2,2,4)

indicators.note: the outer word bears, carries, the others inside

blocks.note: US = American
to pin is to fix in place
an arm is a weapon

annotation.surface: Americans on the warpath attach weapons, with a pun on 'bears' and the right to bear arms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bears' pulls towards the right to bear arms, and it is the instruction for one word to carry the others inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Up in arms means angrily protesting, on the warpath.

entries.clue: Saint with God for eternal youth (5,3)

blocks.note: St Peter, the apostle
Pan, the Greek god of the wild

annotation.surface: A saint teams up with a god in pursuit of everlasting youth.
annotation.walkthrough: The religious surface hides a children's story; Peter Pan is J. M. Barrie's boy who never grows up.
annotation.definitionFit: Peter Pan never grows up, so he stands for eternal youth.

entries.clue: Redo it with changes this boss may require? (6)

blocks.note: anagram fodder
surface padding: it ties the rewrite to the boss who asks for it

annotation.surface: A demanding boss sends the work back: redo it with changes.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is what an editor says, so the definition and the anagram describe the same scene.
annotation.definitionFit: An editor is the boss of a publication who asks writers for rewrites.

entries.clue: Number one Republican in dark film genre (4)

blocks.note: no. is short for number
I is the Roman numeral for one
R = Republican

annotation.surface: The lead Republican appears in a gloomy crime film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Number one' reads as a single idea, the leader, but it splits into NO and I.
annotation.definitionFit: Film noir is the shadowy crime-film genre of 1940s Hollywood.

blocks.note: a nob is a posh, wealthy person in British slang
all = completely, as in 'all alone'

annotation.surface: An exclamation that someone is extraordinarily rich.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extra' reads as 'very', but it is a cricket term: a no ball is an illegal delivery, and the run it gives away is an extra.
annotation.definitionFit: In cricket a no ball concedes a run to the batting side, counted among the extras.

blocks.note: a commercial is an ad
a rift is a break, a split

annotation.surface: The TV ad break seems to have no point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Commercial break' is a set phrase for the adverts on TV, which hides that the two words give separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Adrift means aimless, without direction or purpose.

entries.clue: Pathetic sort died: requiescat in pace (4)

blocks.note: d. = died, as in genealogies
RIP abbreviates the Latin 'requiescat in pace', rest in peace

annotation.surface: A gravestone for a feeble person who has died.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an unkind epitaph, which makes 'Pathetic sort' look like a comment rather than the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A drip is informal for a feeble, dull person.

entries.clue: Oxygen in small amount one disliked (4)

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

blocks.note: a tad is a small amount
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

annotation.surface: A little oxygen goes to someone nobody likes.
annotation.walkthrough: A toad is an informal word for a loathsome person, so 'one disliked' is a fair definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Calling someone a toad means they are repellent and disliked.

entries.clue: Zoom lens? Way to capture insect by river (6)

blocks.note: a spider's web is how it catches insects
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

annotation.surface: A camera question, then a nature scene of a spider trapping a bug beside a river.
annotation.walkthrough: A zoom lens is a camera part, but Zoom is the video-call app, and its lens is a webcam.
annotation.definitionFit: On a Zoom call you are seen through a webcam, so it is the Zoom lens.

entries.clue: Legendary menace fouled Man U trio (8)

indicators.note: fouled means messed up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Three Manchester United players commit fouls and become the menace of legend.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fouled' belongs in a football report, where it means tackled illegally; here it means scrambled. Man U is Manchester United football club.
annotation.definitionFit: The Minotaur was the bull-headed monster of Greek legend in the Cretan labyrinth.

indicators.note: the word lacks the letter that follows

blocks.note: a blimp is a non-rigid airship
b. is the abbreviation for breadth, the letter taken away

annotation.surface: A floppy airship that is too narrow.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Non-rigid airship' is the textbook description of a blimp, so the definition word seems to belong to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something limp flops because it has no stiffness, exactly what a blimp lacks.
